title: FIFA World Cup 2026: Spain crowned champions
text:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup, the first to be hosted jointly by three nations, ran for 39 days from 11 June to 19 July 2026. It was also the first edition expanded to 48 teams, split into 12 groups of four, and featured a record 104 matches across 16 host cities, of which 11 were in the United States, three in Mexico and two in Canada. The opening game on 11 June was played at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, where Mexico beat South Africa 2-0 through goals from Julian Quinones and Raul Jimenez. The match produced three red cards, the most in any World Cup opener, and ended a run of seven World Cup openers in which the Mexicans had failed to win. The same stadium thereby became the first in football history to stage matches at three different World Cups.

The tournament ended on 19 July at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, where Spain defeated defending champion Argentina 1-0 after extra time before a crowd of 80,663. Ferran Torres scored the only goal 39 seconds into the second period of extra time, in the 106th minute, turning in a low cross from Nico Williams. Argentina had been reduced to ten men late in normal time when Enzo Fernandez received a second yellow card, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez made 11 saves, a record for a World Cup final, without being able to deny Spain. The victory gave Spain its second world title and denied Argentina a fourth.

Spain also dominated the individual honours announced after the final. Midfielder Rodri was named winner of the Golden Ball as the best player of the tournament, while goalkeeper Unai Simon took the Golden Glove after conceding just one goal in eight matches. Pau Cubarsi was named best young player, and the Fair Play award went to the Netherlands. The Golden Boot, however, went to France's Kylian Mbappe, who scored 10 goals in eight matches and finished two clear of the second-placed finisher on eight goals. Jude Bellingham and Erling Haaland tied for third place with seven goals each.

The Golden Ball, Golden Glove and Best Young Player awards are chosen by media votes from a shortlist drawn up by FIFA's Technical Study Group. For Mbappe, the award extended a remarkable run at the sport's biggest event: he became the first player to win the top scorer award at two consecutive World Cups. For Spain, whose squad blended experienced campaigners with teenage talent, the result capped a tournament in which its defence was breached only once. The tournament's expanded format meant that the eventual champion had to navigate a new round of 32, introduced because the top two sides from every group and the eight best third-placed teams advanced.

questions.q: Spain's win over Argentina in the 2026 final was its second World Cup title. In which year did Spain win its first, beating the Netherlands 1-0 after extra time?
questions.explanation: Spain won its first World Cup on 11 July 2010 at Soccer City, Johannesburg, beating the Netherlands 1-0 after extra time through an Andres Iniesta goal.

questions.q: Argentina entered the 2026 final as defending champion. Which player won the Golden Ball at the 2022 World Cup, and remains the only player to have won that award twice?
questions.explanation: Lionel Messi was awarded the Golden Ball at the 2022 World Cup (he had also won it in 2014) and is the only player to receive it twice. Mbappe won the 2022 Golden Boot instead.

questions.assertion: The Estadio Azteca in Mexico City became the first stadium in football history to host matches at three different FIFA World Cups when the 2026 tournament opened there.
questions.reason: The Estadio Azteca had earlier hosted World Cup matches in 1970 and 1986.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. The Azteca had hosted matches at the 1970 and 1986 World Cups, so the 2026 opener made it the first stadium to stage matches at three different World Cups; the earlier two editions are exactly what makes 2026 its third.

The 2010 final (Spain v Netherlands) was at Soccer City, Johannesburg; the 2022 final (Argentina v France) at Lusail Stadium, Qatar; the 2026 final at MetLife Stadium; and the 2026 opener at the Estadio Azteca.

statements: I. Kylian Mbappe won the Golden Boot at the 2022 World Cup with eight goals.
II. Argentina beat France in the 2022 final in regulation time, 2-1, without the need for extra time.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: Mbappe scored eight goals in 2022, including a hat-trick in the final. Statement II is incorrect: the 2022 final finished 3-3 after extra time and Argentina won 4-2 on penalties.

statements: 1. The FIFA World Cup trophy was designed by the Italian sculptor Silvio Gazzaniga.
2. The trophy is made of 18-carat gold.
4. The trophy is solid gold throughout, with no hollow interior.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: the trophy is hollow, which is why it weighs about 6.175 kg rather than the 70-80 kg a solid gold version would.
